en: One Scroll of the Method for Reciting the *Avīśa* Spoken by the Deva Maheśvara, with Swift Manifestation of Efficacy.
Compiled by Su Guo,
Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Special Advancement, and Peer of the Third Order of the Opening Prefecture.

The Imperially Enfeoffed Lord of Three Thousand Households, invested with the purple robe and posthumously honored as Minister of Works, bearing the posthumous title "Great Mirror" (Dajian) and the honorific "Great Universal Wisdom" (Dayangzhi), the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery, translated by imperial decree. At that time, the deity Nārāyaṇa...
He was on the summit of Mount Gandhamādana;
having invited Maheśvara to his palace of Īśāna,
he made offerings and prostrated himself at his feet.
He addressed Maheshvara, saying,
"The garuḍa messenger upon whom I ride is able to accomplish whatever essential matters are sought by the world."
Furthermore, it is not swift;
we only pray that Mahādeva will, for the sake of sentient beings in the future,
explain the *āveśa* rite for swiftly establishing proof.
Then Maheśvara addressed Nārāyaṇa, saying:
"Listen attentively;
I shall proclaim for you the method for swiftly accomplishing the task of a messenger."
It can perform the rites of pacification, enrichment, subjugation, and magnetizing;
it can also travel to and fro and serve within the realm of Yāma;
and it can know the future—good and evil, fortune and misfortune, success and failure.
If one wishes to know future events— such as irregularities in drought and flood,
incursions and disturbances from neighboring states, the rebellion of wicked people,
and various other omens of calamity— then [one should proceed].
One should select four or five boys or girls,
approximately seven or eight years of age,
whose bodies are free from scars, moles, or marks.
The practitioner should be intelligent and of keen faculties.
First, have them consume a vegetarian diet for one week or three days.
Whenever one intends to perform the ritual procedure:
One must select an auspicious day, such as when the lunar mansion of Ghost (Ārdrā) or the lunar mansion of Age (Kṛttikā) is in conjunction with the solar day.
A day in conjunction with the lunar mansion of Nectar (Amṛta) is most excellent.
One should bathe the entire body and apply fragrant unguents.
Wearing clean garments and holding camphor and cardamom in the mouth,
the reciter sits facing east. Before him,
he should smear a small altar with white sandalwood incense.
It should be one cubit in measure.
Have young girls stand upon the altar and scatter flowers before them.
Place an *argha* burner and take *guggulu* incense;
empower it seven times with the Great Seal mantra and burn it,
allowing the young girl to fumigate her hands.
Furthermore, take red flowers and empower them seven times;
place them in the palm of a young girl and have her cover her face with her hands.
Then the reciter forms the Great Seal (mahāmudrā):
with the two hands joined in *añjali*, the fingers are interlaced with the left hand pressing over the right; when the palms are thus hollowed, it is accomplished.
With this mudrā, empower one’s own body at five locations:
namely, the forehead, the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the heart, and the throat.
Then, releasing the mudrā upon the crown of the head, recite the mantra as follows:
*Namo bhagavatyai mahāmudrā-khaṭvāṅga-śikhari-śikharo-cce niḥśani-paśupati svāhā.* With this mudrā, press it upon the crown of the girl’s head.
Then, one should visualize above the head a triangular,
crimson-colored, blazing wheel of fire;
recite the mantra seven times while visualizing its light.
The Fire Wheel Mantra is:
Oṃ agniṣe svāhā. Then, with this mudrā, press it upon the mouth of the young girl.
Visualize a white, crescent-shaped water wheel within his mouth;
recite the mantra seven times.
The mantra is: Oṃ jvala-jvālini mani svāhā. Next, one should move the seal and press it upon the center of his heart.
Visualize the earth mandala as square and yellow in shape.
Recite the mantra seven times:
Oṃ mahā-maṇi-parigraha svāhā. Next, one should move the mudrā and press it upon the navel.
Visualize a wind-wheel, circular in shape and black in color.
Recite the mantra seven times:
Oṃ vātā-kula-nātha svāhā. Next, one should empower both feet with the Great Seal (mahāmudrā).
Visualizing oneself as a Garuḍa, recite the mantra:
Oṃ bakṣira jvāla-pāśa svāhā. Next, one should recite the armor mantra while forming the great mudrā.
Empower the young girl by rotating [the mantra] over her entire body. The mantra is:
Oṃ kavaca-mahānta-dīpa-te svāhā. Next, the practitioner should visualize themselves as the deity Maheśvara.
Adorned with a three-eyed crown and necklaces,
there is a Buddha and a crescent moon upon the crown;
the neck is blue.
He has eighteen arms, holding various weapons,
with a dragon serving as his sash.
He binds it with cross-straps;
furthermore, having smeared it with blood and written [the mantra] upon it,
he contemplates his own body for a brief moment.
Next, one should protect the hundred and eight vital points (*prāṇa-sthāna*) of that maiden with the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*). The mantra is:
Oṃ mṛtyuvañcana-jīvaka-jaḥ. While forming this Great Seal and reciting the mantra, [one should perform the protection].
Circumambulate the entire body while performing the empowerment;
this shall protect the one hundred and eight vital joints.
Next, again employ the Great Seal.
Consecrate the fragrant flowers, the *argha* water, and other offerings with mantras.
Next, bind the boundaries of the ten directions using the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) mantra.
Then, one should stand before this young girl.
The mantra for reciting the Mahesvara Messenger is as follows:

*Lijitaka* (1) *mādana* (2) *viśanabhaṇa* (3) *samnāgara* (4) *vikrama* (5) *vilasagati* (6) *rijitaka* (7) *pralipadāṇam* (8) *cara cara* (9) *cari cari* (10) *bhaṇa bhaṇa* (11) *bhani bhani* (12) *bandhe bandhe* (13) *kaṭhi kaṭhi* (14) *avisa avisa* (15) *rijitaka* (16) *ruṇuñciñjavati svāhā* (17). This mantra should be recited seven times.
Then that maiden will tremble;
know that the Noble One has entered her body.
Then, snap the fingers once more and recite the mantra.
If no immediate sign of efficacy appears, next recite the mantra for subjugating the messengers (*dūta*), which is as follows:

*ṛṣi ṛṣaye marukhita svara svara purdahana hana parāhaṃmanani naduruni dūrini muṇi muṇi baṃri baṃri kaṭhi kaṭhi avīśa avīśa ṛṣiṭaka runuñciñcapadyate svāhā*. By reciting this mantra, a swift response will certainly be obtained.
If one asks about future good or evil, or all manner of portents and omens,
and the deity remains silent or speaks with delay,
then one should form the staff mudrā.
Join the two palms together.
Extend the two ring fingers outward.
Place the two middle fingers side by side.
Hook the tips of the two index fingers with the two ring fingers,
and press the two thumbs against each other so that they cross at the center.
Recite the mantra as follows:
Oṃ munigara duru duru svāhā. Having thus bound this staff-seal (daṇḍamudrā), one then speaks and asks about various matters.
Consecrate the arghya with the Mahāmudrā mantra and sprinkle it three times upon the face of the young girl; then,
immediately perform the binding and releasing of the mudrās.
One should first recite this messenger’s mantra ten thousand times, and then the rite will be accomplished;
the deity will appear in bodily form.
One must then offer argha water and make a request for boons.
"May the Noble One accomplish all tasks in all places and at all times.
Having said this, [the object] disappears and does not appear. Later, when one wishes to employ it, [it reappears].
Anoint a small altar, place incense, flowers, food, and drink upon it,
and recite the mantra one hundred and eight times;
then [the deity] will manifest in person.
Thus it is said that one takes long-life elixirs and wish-fulfilling jewels from within the dragon palaces,
or causes them to be obtained from the realm of King Yāma,
thereby extending one's life and increasing one's lifespan.
It may cause one to obtain sublime nectar from above;
it may send messengers to other kingdoms to inquire about their virtues and vices;
and it can also assist military arrays in crushing and defeating external enemies.
All various applications can be accomplished by this;
it is the most supreme among all garuḍa rites,
secret and difficult to obtain.
You should carefully discern those who are vessels worthy of receiving the transmission and bestow it upon them;
for if one gives it to those who are not vessels,
it will harm others and this Dharma will fail to flourish hereafter.
Therefore, you should keep this strictly secret and not transmit or receive it recklessly.
The *dhāraṇī* of Maheśvara-Garuḍa is as follows:

*Namo bhagavate rudrāya cchinnakaparāya sarvavidyāñjanakarāya sarvakarmasādhakāya sarvavaśīkaraṇāya sarvasattvavināśanāya oṃ kaparajita chinnakapabodha ruṇṭuṅkiñjapāyate svāhā.* This is the *dhāraṇī*.
To subdue a person, draw that person using red plantain leaves;
write their name upon their heart and recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times.
If one buries [the object] in cow dung, it will be immediately subdued.
If one wishes to cause a son-in-law and his wife to hate each other,
one should draw the forms of that man and woman on *tāla* leaves.
Write the names [of the persons] facing each other.
Take thread and wrap it around them.
Take the fur of a weasel, the feathers of a mountain pheasant, and sloughed snake skin; burn them as incense.
Recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times,
place it inside a karpāsa cloth,
and immediately bury it within a cemetery.
They will then harbor mutual hatred;
let them be removed and restored to their former state, so that they may feel mutual compassion.
Then, draw the figure of that husband upon a tāla leaf,
write his name together with hers,
and bind them with white thread.
Take the feathers of a sparrow and the skin of a snake, burn them as incense,
and recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times;
they will immediately feel compassion for one another.
Furthermore, if one wishes to cause people to fight,
one should draw two persons grasping each other by their topknots upon a tiger skin or an ox hide.
Tie a book with thread and place it over a fire until it is heavy.
Bury it beneath the mortar;
then you will be able to strike each other every day until the end of the kalpa.
Furthermore, according to another method, if one wishes to subjugate a person,
one should take a *paṭola* leaf and draw the figure of that person upon it.
Write their name and recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times.
One should immediately bury it beneath the bed;
thus, [the affliction] will be subdued.
Furthermore, there is a rite for those suffering from hematuria.
Take a tāla leaf and draw that person upon it,
writing their name.
Take a nail and recite the dhāraṇī one hundred and eight times over it.
If one nails it down for seven weeks,
it will be removed immediately.
Next, the method for eye medicine is explained.
If one wishes to subdue a stubborn person,
one should take the head of a snake, *kharāśana*, blue sandalwood (*nīlacandana*), *likṣā* (lac), and beeswax;
on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, these should be ground together into a powder.
They smear their corners of the eyes with meat-paste;
all these wretches follow after him,
coming from the heavens as well, not merely from the human realm.
One fascicle of the *Magheshvara-deva-proktakalaviraviśa-dharmā* (The Method of the Kālaviṛāvaṃśa Spoken by the Deva Maheśvara), which Swiftly Establishes Efficacy.
